rationale: Cheap unconditional exile also answers dormant Spacecraft; giving a basic to hand is a real but modest drawback.
First copy can generate multiple cards; 3/1 body trades with Officer tokens so copies and artifact payoffs matter more than combat.
Efficient defensive body and repeatable Borg production; evasion from Organic Avulsion Unit or Locutus turns contact into a growing board.
Two artifact bodies for two mana enable affinity, sacrifice, team buffs and profitable beam-me-up replays.
Lifelink stabilizes early; station taps enable the counter replacement before charging ships or growing creatures.
Two-drop produces bodies from modal spells and modal creature triggers; five-color activated ability is a rare late bonus.
Three-mana anthem plus a token for every creature or Spacecraft spell immediately snowballs; tutor is optional upside rather than necessary.
Cheap answer to large creatures and completed ships, with a cantrip floor that also triggers dilemma payoffs.
Two-power artifact one-drop supports aggressive Borg decks; vigilance preserves blockers and station opportunities.
Three-mana setup recoups value with two nontoken artifacts; high artifact density supports it, but token artifacts do not trigger it.
Efficient two-drop adds permanent stats to every subsequent creature and token; strong with go-wide plans and beam replays.
Solid evasive artifact body; untap ability lets a creature station and still attack, or station two ships in one turn.
No built-in lifegain, but each Medic, lifelink, Food or dual-land event adds two counters because Crusher doubles her own trigger; beam can repeat those events.
Initial body is small for four mana, but saves countered creatures repeatedly and pairs with distributed counters and Doctor EMH.
Can be a one-mana artifact 1/2 or place the counter on a better body; attractive beam fuel and counter enabler but low standalone impact.
Six-mana 6/6 adds multiple bodies immediately; death triggers distribute counters and turn chump blocks into lasting board strength.
Often a four-mana vigilance body plus card, since any permanent counter qualifies; modal ETB is especially good to replay.
Selection rather than advantage on first cast; improves when tutoring a bomb ship and replaying a value creature, but consumes considerable mana.
Landcycling prevents early dead draws; large artifact body and temporary team boost support go-wide attacks.
Efficient flyer with repeatable value when paired with beam recursion; blink reuses strong ETBs and resets problematic enchantments.
Three-mana 3/3 artifact with a realistic eight-total-power payoff; Spacecraft eventually help meet the threshold.
Three-mana Oblivion Ring with ward and artifact synergies; answers almost every bomb, including dormant ships and engines.
Temporary exile is not permanent removal; can instead blink a friendly ETB creature, and the Clue provides eventual material.
ETB can immediately draw at end step; repeated beam casts draw additional cards and the body is efficiently sized.
Requires sacrificing a creature and leaving mana open; powerful team protection only when already developed, with little proactive value.
Fixes the next land drop and supplies an artifact; six station counters are substantial for only a 2/2 flyer, so assess chiefly as a land finder.
Opponent chooses whether to skip combat; four-mana symmetrical draw engine rarely reaches twelve counters before decisive combat or removal.
Good three-mana power for station and eight-power attacks; needs a partner to attack and trades down into small blockers.
Reusable power boost can improve combat or station output, but sorcery timing and tapping the source constrain defense and tempo.
Borg double strike creates large immediate attacks with even modest artifact boards; fragile body and four-mana cost keep it below the best bombs.
Counters spread efficiently and recur through beam; strong with lifelink and counter payoffs, but returning a creature is not free board development.
Six-card artifact selection is likely to replace itself in this environment; body and subsequent counters make a reliable value creature.
Flash creature usually removes an attacker using existing diverse types; five mana and Borg-heavy boards reduce consistency.
One-mana defensive removal or proactive stun is flexible; targets an attacker for damage and cannot permanently kill larger creatures.
Protection plus permanent counter wins combat and protects high-value engines; can also save a dormant Spacecraft.
Five-mana evasive attacker stabilizes with lifegain; stationing also triggers the life, but cannot fly when blocking.
First-strike two-drop with a conditional draw engine; sequencing equipment or ships before attacking or stationing makes the condition attainable.
Fragile early body; eight-power attack condition comes later, but accumulated counters and untapping help offensive boards.
Two-mana permanent team boost is excellent with Borg and Officer tokens; draw mode prevents dead hands but gives opponent a card.
Selects land or a cheap permanent with high hit rate; beam provides late value and ETB reuse without being an immediate extra card.
Exponential 0/1 tokens cannot block and need a power anthem or sacrifice payoff; too much setup for an ordinary deck.
Durable five-drop makes attacks difficult to block after the eight-power threshold; no ETB value or independent evasion.
Three bodies immediately stabilize and charge the ship over two turns; ward plus a 5/5 flying lifelinker is a powerful endgame.
Four-mana removal spell with a later 4/4 flyer attached; destroy target tapped creature can miss defensive engines and requires a legal target.
Efficient artifact body with useful tempo ETB; tap effect is especially valuable to replay when attacking with Borg.
Noncreature spells include ships and artifacts; first two triggers filter, later triggers generate cards, but the setup costs a turn without a body.
Large vigilant ward body stabilizes; subsequent modal spells generate free opposing spells, including on opposing turns with instant dilemmas.
Ward protects a body that permanently grows with noncreature casts; strong if deployed before the spell-heavy turns, slower than cheap threats.
Usually costs five or six rather than nine; two bodies plus net card advantage are substantial, but unique-land requirements delay it.
Flash two-drop trades while filtering a card; excellent replay target for beam and helps fill the graveyard.
Soft counter remains useful because the other mode replaces itself and buys a combat step; reliably triggers dilemma abilities.
Starts vulnerable but naturally grows each draw step and scales sharply with draw-two spells and beam cantrips.
Six-mana draw-only spell needs several unique land names to outperform cheaper draw spells and adds no board presence.
Copies best artifact or creature with counters intact and removes legendary restriction; can copy an already-stationed ship or either player's bomb.
Good defensive stats and modal ETB; either recovers a ship or fills the graveyard and sets up draws, with profitable beam replays.
Cheap tempo and a second cast; sorcery timing and opponent ETB creatures constrain it, while returning your own creature can create value.
Defensive body usually finds a playable opposing land among several cards; no extra land drop, and off-color lands mostly support unique names.
ETB delays an attacker before becoming an evasive vigilant threat; station six still requires real creature taps.
Cheap flying artifact with modal ETB; enables dilemma and artifact engines and is easy to beam, though the unassisted body is small.
Instant broadly answers creatures or dormant ships; cheaper against attackers, but top-library option gives opponent a redraw.
Baseline two-mana 2/2 leaves Equipment after removal; token-copy ability is situational and still requires paying equip costs.
Four-mana hard counter with occasional two-mana use; holding up four is costly against value creatures and cheap spell chains.
Whale tutor has common targets and gives immediate value; draw and extra-turn payoffs require charging eight counters and connecting.
Five-mana 3/3 usually finds one card from a useful selection; counts her own two types, but Borg boards reduce selection depth.
Landcycling keeps it useful early; large vigilant ward body defends well but lacks evasion and immediate card advantage.
Bounce attached to four power is useful tempo and a good beam target; five-mana cost and opposing ETBs limit repeated bouncing.
Repeated modal creature triggers grow Jett; station provides safe surveils and eventually draws once power reaches four.
Fourth upkeep forces losing the game; needs a fast win or a specific blink or sacrifice outlet, so nominal draw and token value overstates reliability.
Both players' noncreature spells grow Data; surplus counters become cheap cards, with counter removal available from all friendly creatures.
Three power supports station even without text; doubling charge counters accelerates Spacecraft significantly but requires a supporting board.
Four-mana draw two plus Officer is reliable material and dilemma support; untap mode occasionally completes a ship or generates mana instead.
Cheap disabling Aura can wait for a creature to tap; paying four taps immediately, and beam prevention closes a major escape route.
Flying vigilance threat grows with each dilemma, including modal ETB creatures; three mana and one initial toughness expose it to cheap removal.
Doubles every draw, including routine draw steps and draw-two spells; four-toughness body survives small damage and the advantage snowballs rapidly.
Three-mana 2/4 is an effective blocker; choosing a common mana value generates extra cards as opponent develops, though late deployment is worse.
Cheap spell for noncreature engines and a later beam cast; returning a value creature is useful but must be repaid in mana and tempo.
Low initial cost with hexproof while dormant; noncreature casts help reach eight counters without forfeiting all creature attacks.
Steal mode gives opponent three cards; gifting a disposable token for draw three is often better, but five-mana timing and material costs matter.
Reuses instant and sorcery cards at normal mana cost while returning ETB creatures; main-phase restriction prevents instant-speed protection loops.
Two-mana 0/4 blocks while looting every turn; five unique lands eventually unlock extra cards, while the seven-name transformation is a remote bonus.
Efficient defensive body and three station power; noncreature-heavy decks can attack often, but it cannot attack without casting a spell first.
Flash body with modal stun gives flexible tempo and dilemma triggers; Stifle mode is narrower than countering a spell.
Immediate card replaces the investment; five station counters are relatively attainable for a 3/2 flyer and artifact ETB synergies add value.
Three-power creature becomes a reasonably cheap repeatable tapper once three or four distinct lands are established.
Selection cantrip is a useful floor and delayed blink protects or reuses creatures; only one mode is chosen, so protection does not also draw.
Looting fills the graveyard for beam, then chapter two recovers a useful card; third chapter adds little immediate material.
Seven-mana flyer replaces itself on entry and keeps drawing or weakens attackers; expensive without cycling but closes stalled games.
One mana grants two persistent opposing cards with mana flexibility while giving opponent one of yours; no short play deadline, but symmetrical resources matter.
Flash 2/2 chooses two useful effects; bounce is restricted to mana value two or less and the draw mode is filtering rather than advantage.
Can generate extra artifact cards from the library top and gives every ship two counters; benefits from high artifact density without needing a ship immediately.
Discard mode is instant-speed three-mana -4/-4; late 6/6 menace strips hands every end step, giving useful early and late halves.
Artifact lord improves its own power and wide Borg boards; four mana for a defensive 3/4 is fair but not a value play.
Three-mana flyer converts disposable artifacts or creatures into cards on attack; Food, Borg tokens and exhausted value artifacts supply fodder.
ETB kills small engines or blockers and leaves a reusable power boost; misses four-toughness creatures and costs mana to equip later.
Menace threat grows from either player's creature deaths, once each turn; token exchanges and sacrifice make growth consistent after the weak initial turn.
Flying body can reuse a cheap creature ETB immediately and gains drain from graveyard departures; requires a suitable graveyard target for full value.
Six power across two bodies for five mana, including a hasty token; valuable with Klingon sacrifice and excellent to replay through beam.
Cheap artifact body enables card drawing by tapping three artifact creatures; competes with station and attacks but works with summoning-sick tokens.
Low-cost Borg scales in power with the artifact-creature board, both attacking and charging ships; two toughness remains vulnerable.
Three-mana 3/2 with either a Clue or graveyard interaction; repeated modal ETBs support dilemmas and beam value.
Modal ETB either sweeps tokens or edicts; sacrifice mode is symmetrical but can sacrifice itself, and opponents can exploit expendable tokens.
Eight-mana engine immediately reanimates at end step and gives Borg indestructible; very strong when cast but often stranded before then.
Five-mana scalable sweeper normally clears small and medium creatures; six unique names for bonus tokens is uncommon.
Usually neutralizes an attacker and removes blocking immediately; artifact or creature activated engines remain functional until threshold exile.
Two-mana instant kills small creatures, or sacrifices a cheap artifact to kill almost any large creature; abundant expendable material supports kicker.
Efficient menace 3/3 plus repeatable four-point life swings from modal spells and creature abilities; threatens quick wins while stabilizing.
Early discard is real card advantage and can be repeated via beam; three-power one-toughness body trades down against tokens.
Large menace threat returns cheaply from graveyard after a dilemma, making ordinary trades favorable; five-mana replay cost still matters.
One-mana sacrifice outlet grows every Klingon permanently, including itself; token Klingons and multiple cheap Warriors create explosive combat.
Six-mana durable blocker draws at each end step and prevents life-total losses while alive; removing it at negative life is a serious vulnerability.
Cheap power trick replaces itself only if the target dies; cannot save a creature and is awkward against exile, bounce or noncombat engines.
Accumulates Treasures on either player's creature deaths and grows from them; starts small but supports ramp, splashes and sacrifice decks.
Seven-mana menace bomb doubles opposing life loss each end step and gains that life; triple black and no reliable entry removal limit consistency.
Unconditional instant removal with surveil is reliable; four mana is less efficient than the best two-mana answers.
A sturdy artifact body grants card draw to the whole Borg board on contact; menace and token swarms turn it into substantial advantage.
Instant draw two is a solid floor; removal creates two opposing tokens, so best used on bombs rather than routine creatures.
Nontoken edict, Clue and later two bodies supply sustained material; five-mana initial investment can be punished by wide boards.
Three-power two-drop is serviceable but one toughness trades poorly; blind naming rarely shuts off the opponent's most relevant card.
Four-mana five-power body turns a disposable artifact or token into two cards immediately; casting from exile is useful additional resilience.
Five toughness stalls ground attacks and modal chains drain repeatedly; low power and four-mana cost make it a defensive synergy piece.
Efficient artifact body and repeatable team menace; creates attacks for Borg card-draw and token-generation lords.
Efficient Borg body repeatedly recasts artifact creatures from the graveyard; finality limits infinite recycling but each recovery is valuable.
Selection, self-mill and a cheap second cast; gains value with ETB creatures and graveyard payoffs but first casting does not add cards.
Small lifelink artifact can trade or be sacrificed and later replaces itself; weak damage output and three-mana graveyard draw keep it modest.
Two-mana kill spell misses many Borg and other artifact creatures, but reanimation mode supplies a good alternative in artifact-heavy matchups.
Landcycling fixes early hands; large artifact body either stabilizes life or filters the next draws, with a modal trigger on entry.
Efficient lifelink two-drop disrupts a specific opposing card but replaces it; knowledge and lifegain matter more than raw card advantage.
First attack can immediately create a 2/2 if your own graveyard has a card; beam, cycling and graveyard activations provide additional token triggers.
Aggressive one-drop returns once through finality; supports Klingons and sacrifice but cannot stabilize by blocking.
Three-mana two-card recursion is useful after trades; hand-exile mode gives an early use and both modes trigger dilemmas.
Attack trigger faces a dilemma every turn and can grant deathtouch to itself or another attacker; excellent support for repeated modal payoffs.
Opponent controls the initial outcome and replay costs mana; repeated drain can matter with dilemmas but it adds no board and can be denied cards.
Two artifact bodies across a death trigger for two mana; ideal for Borg lords, sacrifice, affinity and graveyard recasting.
One-mana modal cantrip or creature recovery; cheap dilemma enabler with a decent late-game floor but no inherent card advantage.
Four-mana reanimation provides immediate value and the returned creature helps charge the ship; ten counters delay the recurring attack payoff.
Every creature death drains but three-mana setup does not affect the board; relies on sustained exchanges or a sacrifice engine.
Noncreature casts produce permanent Officers and grow the Instructor's power; ships and reusable beam spells make repeated triggers realistic.
First strike makes a useful aggressive two-drop; tapping for station also builds toward the occasional two-damage trigger.
Hasty Klingon token contributes to sacrifice and tribal plans; beam provides a later body and value-creature replay at a tempo cost.
Opponent can decline the exile when your free spell is weak or unavailable; double red and noncreature restriction make this unreliable interaction.
Reasonable defensive stats and a recurring power boost; eight-total-power condition later makes a key attacker harder to block.
Immediate modal token or filtering and repeated attack triggers generate advantage; empty-hand mode selection turns it into a powerful army engine.
Efficient trample body supplies damage on normal land drops; ramp and fetch effects add counters with second landfall triggers.
Flash first strike can win one combat, but the Aura remains exposed to two-for-one removal and supplies no toughness thereafter.
Three station power turns this cheap ship into a free hasty Klingon each combat; those tokens can later help charge it or be sacrificed.
Four-power body can sacrifice an exhausted artifact, spare token or enchantment for two damage to any target; profitable ETB replay target.
Temporary copies can exploit ETBs or finish games, but triple red and dependence on opposing creatures make the card inconsistent.
Instant draw-two impulse gives a floor while two damage to all creatures can sweep tokens; double red and symmetrical damage require care.
Hasty body repeatedly produces extra landfall triggers and temporary mana; returned land can be replayed, but natural land drops are still required.
Recurring landfall selection has a high ceiling; four-mana setup and same-turn play permission often waste the first revealed spell.
Six damage answers most creatures; replacing your land with New Planet can improve fixing, distinct names and landfall, but five mana is slow.
Large trampling finisher with an early landcycling option; lacks entry value, protection or immediate haste.
Nine mana plus a graveyard spell and a diverse surviving board is excessive setup; poor when behind or drawn early.
Scalable instant removal efficiently kills four-toughness creatures for three mana and exiles recursion targets; cannot damage players.
Five-power trample body immediately clears Officer and Borg tokens and small engines while leaving your own board intact.
Good power and useful attack payoff, but requires eight total power and has no protective or card-advantage ETB.
Efficient basic body; doubling another creature's future triggers costs two mana and removes this creature from attacks or station.
Three-power trampler for two mana trades up and leaves a one-damage trigger that can finish another creature or hit a player.
Temporary ramp must be used on a narrow chapter-two window, and chapter three sacrifices a land; poor lasting material without specific sequencing.
Haste and first strike combine with immediate team power boost to threaten lethal; seven mana requires a deck able to reach its finishing turn.
Instant artifact destruction hits Borg, ships and engines; substantial pump mode provides a broadly useful alternative and a dilemma trigger.
One-mana removal is efficient against small creatures and tokens; four-damage upgrade requires a prior death and is not always available.
Usually attacks as a three-power two-drop while land drops continue; lacks lasting growth or entry value.
Instant three damage to any target with optional filtering; handles engines, finishes combat and turns surplus lands into new cards.
Four-mana 4/4 offers persistent replacement of bad hand cards with one sampled spell; copies still require paying mana and consume a card from hand.
Treasure tokens cannot be sacrificed while Quark remains; bounce can eventually unlock stored mana, but the small body and unsupported tokens are poor alone.
Graveyard spells reduce cost of a flying hasty threat; beam exiles its own spells, so discount should not assume every cast remains in the graveyard.
Cheap two-card access supports noncreature engines and land drops; delayed permission helps use both cards, but it adds no immediate blocker.
Team power boost can finish wide boards or trade up while blocking; defensive discount does not add toughness or save creatures.
Immediate team power anthem supports tokens and eight-power attacks; ten-counter flying body arrives later, aided by creature deaths.
Two-mana creature ramps into four-drops and banks Treasure later; one toughness is fragile and mana is only red until Treasure production.
Four-power reach body plus a card playable through next turn is reliable top-end material, but five mana competes with stronger ships and bombs.
Cheap haste body can generate a Clue when it dies during your turn; small stats and conditional replacement make it primarily support material.
Three power can station efficiently and untaps after noncreature spells; repeated pings pressure life totals but cannot remove creatures.
Five-power menace is an excellent rate until attacking requires repeated nonland sacrifices; disposable material helps but ongoing card loss is substantial.
Hasty two-drop replaces itself on death with temporary card access, then repeats once from the graveyard; strong sacrifice and graveyard-leaving synergy.
Klingon double strike is a strong trick in the right deck; instant rummage-draw mode supplies a fallback and dilemma trigger.
Two-mana three damage to any target is strong initially; expensive triple-red beam is later value rather than the main reason to draft it.
Four-power body generates two temporary lands every combat, including entry turn; ramp, landfall and thinning all matter despite sacrificing those lands later.
Three-power body plus temporary theft of a cheap opposing creature enables a large attack; free sacrifice outlets can turn theft into permanent removal.
Three-mana four-damage removal with later filtering and a permanent edict; surviving larger creatures can instead be stolen for combat.
Reasonable three-mana artifact body generated by a noncreature spell; beam adds a second body and can reuse an ETB creature.
Fight is conditional but followed by life and creature recovery; three chapters provide value when you can safely win the initial fight.
Ordinary two-drop becomes a four-power creature at a reasonable activation cost as unique names accumulate; once-per-turn restriction prevents an unlimited pump sink.
Eight mana usually yields several tapped permanents but often includes lands; unique-name and high-cost requirements leave many early dead draws.
Three mana supplies four power across two bodies and three creature types; repeatable federation boost supports attacks and station acceleration.
Explores immediately and for every subsequent creature, improving draws or adding counters; additional land play converts explored lands into tempo.
Power grows with unique lands and playing lands off the library provides real card advantage; double green and early two-basic-land boards constrain initial size.
Cycling solves early hands; entry counters create substantial stats or improve an existing threat, and small creatures cannot block it.
Two-mana combined bite can use two friendly creatures to kill a large target without fighting; needs a developed board and can be disrupted.
Normally a four-mana 4/5 with a modal trigger; mana mode enables another spell or a splash while leaving a solid body.
Pump mode is useful, but three mana is expensive and opposing artifact/enchantment edict cannot reliably hit a chosen bomb amid spare artifacts.
Defensive body plus a permanent land token ramps and fixes all colors; excellent to replay through beam, though repeated tokens share one name.
Vigilant 4/4 gives useful station power without sacrificing future blocks; modal surveil or graveyard interaction adds flexibility and dilemma triggers.
Can be a three-mana 4/2 or improve a better creature; trample for countered creatures helps distribute counters and push damage.
Doubles creature counters and protects other countered creatures; strong with Doctors, dilemma growth and landfall, but does not protect itself by default.
Flash body returns a non-Doctor permanent or insures another creature against death; non-Doctor restriction matters but artifact and creature targets are plentiful.
Three-mana ramp finds dual-color Planets as well as basics; cheap beam can ramp again and reuse a creature, at the cost of rebuilding that body.
Instant selection almost always finds a permanent and fills the graveyard; useful consistency rather than raw advantage, with first-spell life a small bonus.
Permanent ramp also counts as an artifact; expensive later activation converts basic lands into utility lands and extra unique names rather than adding land count.
Four mana immediately supplies two 3/3s, then turns Officer, Borg, Food, Clue and even Planet tokens into 3/3 artifacts; token utility is lost but board power is enormous.
Returning a permanent immediately triggers a 3/3 token as well as the 2/2 body; later beam and graveyard departures generate more tokens once each turn.
One-mana trick untaps and supplies a temporary +1/+1 plus permanent counter; supports counter engines and station while remaining combat-efficient.
Two-mana creature grows and produces increasing green mana every first main phase; provides both early acceleration and a scaling body without tapping.
Efficient body gains life from normal land drops and Clues from second landfalls; ramp, Anomalies and temporary land engines improve the draw rate.
Aggressive one-drop replaces targeted removal or combat tricks with an Officer; opponent can still block it and tokens enter tapped.
Cheap deathtouch creature discourages large attackers and can gain reach against ships; weak station power and susceptibility to pings limit it.
Five-mana 6/6 with reach, vigilance and deathtouch dominates many combats and provides station power; no entry card advantage or protection.
Food supplies one reliable growth trigger and later lifegain can grow it further; starts as a low-impact 1/1 and needs mana or supporting cards.
Five-power reach body stabilizes against flyers and charges ships; graveyard token adds value after trading or being milled.
Six mana provides a 5/5 and indestructible chump blocker; team mana arrives late, so do not value it like an early mana engine.
Flash body can save a valuable creature from targeted removal while improving the board; no protection from sweepers or combat damage.
Four-power body attacks larger on landfall and supplies a repeatable late land-token sink; no immediate value if unable to attack.
Large body gains several life and bypasses Borg blockers; six mana and vulnerability to nonartifact removal limit the tribal protection.
Each attack ramps permanently into any color and triggers landfall; three-mana setup adds no blocker and repeated New Planets do not add unique names.
Every later creature receives permanent stats and eventually two counters; slow initial investment but especially effective with repeated creature tokens.
ETB surveil stocks beam spells and graveyard fuel; recurring combat counter costs only one mana and can immediately improve a creature on later turns.
Landfall distributes two permanent counters each turn, creating a rapidly growing team; five-mana initial 4/4 needs a land drop to supply immediate extra value.
Three-mana defensive body replaces itself with a land or Treasure after milling; supports graveyard engines, splashes and beam ETB reuse.
Very cheap artifact/enchantment answer hits many early engines and Borg but misses large ships; graveyard-exile lifegain mode is a weak fallback.
Five mana immediately discovers a real spell and later attacks repeat it; six station counters are attainable and the final body is evasive.
Four-mana double land ramp is substantial and later leaves a flying vigilance ship; eight counters require another board, and entry does not block immediately.
Replaces itself with a land but does not ramp on entry; untapped lands help the many taplands, while the eventual draw activation still needs blue mana.
Two-mana any-color source has three toughness and ramps into powerful four-drops; supports splashes without needing extra off-color lands.
Three-mana body receives permanent counters on ordinary land drops; extra landfall can quickly turn it into a large threat and station resource.
Three draw-two/exile-one chapters generate sustained selection and material, with possible life at the end; five mana in two colors adds no immediate blocker.
Affinity makes entry exile affordable in a Borg deck; later attacks assimilate the exiled creature and twelve counters grant team evasion, but charging still takes a board.
Phases out both boards and uses a fragile token to lock phasing; draw and life buy time, but ending the lock can return opposing creatures before yours.
Hybrid landfall engine makes a 2/2 on every land drop; tokens cannot block, so it is stronger offensively and with sacrifice or repeated land entry.
Hybrid five-drop has an immediate modal ETB: two Clues for material or two stun counters for tempo; strong beam target but expensive.
Efficient gold body generates temporary mana from landfall and later turns surplus lands into cards; sacrificing lands can undo unique-name thresholds.
Hybrid Gravedigger is broadly castable and synergizes with beam; graveyard activation supplies life and a departure trigger after death or self-mill.
Three distinct colors and limited enchantment density constrain the draw engine; Saga-counter activation is useful but cannot justify unsupported casting demands.
Hybrid five-drop is at least a 5/5 when targeting itself and distributes extra counters to the existing countered team; excellent with repeated ETBs.
Two hybrid mana supplies a 3/2 followed by a hasty 2/1 when it dies; excellent Klingon fodder with strong standalone material.
Sturdy hybrid three-drop can untap a mana source, attacker, tap engine or station contributor; surveil is an additional late sink rather than immediate draw.
Free sacrifice outlet grows from all creature deaths; sacrificing Klingons also draws cards, with multiple repeatable Klingon-token sources available.
Hybrid engine copies a creature each combat after a noncreature cast, reusing ETBs and adding a hasty attacker; requires a creature board and spell sequencing.
Efficient gold body loots when attacking or stationing; ship hexproof applies only during your turn, so it does not prevent all opposing removal.
Ramp and team haste combine well with large creatures and landfall; no creature body and three-color-style gold demand keep the floor moderate.
Reanimates a green or white creature immediately, then offers a large combat-draw opportunity; needs a suitable graveyard and a way to connect.
Efficient trampling gold attacker boosts later creatures and turns combat-time tokens into attackers; lacks an immediate token or card itself.
Gold 3/3 supplies attack-card access at eight total power, and a sacrifice option answers artifacts or enchantments; must establish a board to draw reliably.
Seven mana can gain substantial life, but draw scales with cards left in hand and no blocker is created; often too little material when expensive hands finally empty.
Two-mana Borg anthem buffs itself and wide artifact boards; discard-removal mode prevents a dead draw when colors or board are awkward.
Hybrid artifact body either filters two cards or pushes an attacker through; modal ETB and artifact status make it easy to fit into several engines.
Three-mana defensive body creates a temporary Klingon attacker every combat, including entry turn; sacrifice synergies turn those tokens into lasting value.
Three-mana opposing-creature copy with menace scales with the best opposing threat; explicit kicker cost is six additional mana despite a conflicting reminder parenthesis.
Cheap menace threat becomes 3/4 for one mana, surveils when tapped and later replays graveyard lands; upgrades are permanent and can be paid off curve.
Trampling body turns countered creatures' combat damage into cards; needs counters on attackers and can draw multiple cards from a wide successful attack.
Five types for one card is plausible with diverse species and jobs; three-color 0/5 and a board-dependent draw threshold make unsupported hands awkward.
Four-mana 2/4 draws for every dilemma, including repeatable attack abilities and modal ETBs; substantial enabler density makes this a true archetype engine.
Two-mana body digs four for a noncreature nonland spell; spell-heavy UR often replaces it, but the selection can miss in creature-heavy builds.
Two-mana reach vigilance body starts at modest power and scales with distinct lands; three toughness stays fixed and two colors are required early.
Durable three-mana body surveils each upkeep and draws once per turn from graveyard departures; beam and several common graveyard activations supply fuel.
Hybrid one-power creature can grow by tapping spare artifacts or summoning-sick bodies; eight-power attacks double its power but setup taps compete with combat and station.
Symmetrical cards and damage usually leave you down the Saga card without affecting the board; direct draw-growth synergies rarely compensate reliably.
Hybrid lifelink body taxes a chosen opposing hand card by two mana; disruption is temporary rather than permanent exile, but helps protect tempo.
Three-mana any-color rock later becomes a flying vigilant blocker; six station counters require creatures, so the mana function is the dependable floor.
Two Equipment copies need seven total mana to equip two creatures before unblockability works; lacks a stat boost and is slow when behind.
Eight-mana flying 7/7 selectively sweeps nonartifact creatures when cast; strong payoff, but artifact-heavy opposing boards reduce the sweep and early copies are stranded.
Colorless two-drop filters on entry and supports artifact boards; bottom-of-library activation triggers graveyard engines but is otherwise slow card recycling.
Nine-mana entry can immediately add several permanents and repeats each upkeep; mana cost is extreme and lands or dormant ships do not always stabilize at once.
Flexible sunburst sweeper can clear token swarms or a chosen low mana-value band; color access limits the maximum, and the effect is symmetrical.
Seven-mana artifact requires further mana to replay one permanent each turn; sideboard access helps selection but it usually lacks an immediate stabilizing play.
Two-mana artifact ramp is restricted to artifacts and their abilities; looting is useful later and helps noncreature engines, but does not generate extra cards.
Food provides an initial token and repeatable copying grows a board with Borg, Officers or Illusions; copying Food alone is not fast board development.
Five-mana artifact can put its first counter on a creature immediately; lifegain and later entries improve the rate, but it needs a surviving creature and time.
Replaces itself on entry and leaves artifact fodder or a modal sacrifice activation; especially useful with dilemma payoffs and cheap artifact sacrifice.
